newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Emirates and Virgin Atlantic airlines emerge as two main bidders to purchase a 40 percent stake of national carrier Airlanka.
Tamil Nadu chief minister Mutuvel Karunanidhi says he will not extend any support to Sri Lanka's separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
Police arrest trade union leaders as workers at the former government-owned Ceylon Steel Corporation protest against the sale of the company to Korea's Hanjung.
At least 37 killed in attack on security forces camp at Pulukunava in eastern Batticaloa district by LTTE rebels.

The People's Liberation Front (JVP) is dedicated to working within a democratic framework, the previously radical leftist organisation's leader Tilwin de Silva says. Two insurgencies by the JVP brought the country to a standstill in 1971 and in the late 1980s.
Forty six Tamil Tigers and 38 security forces personnel killed in attack on eastern army camp by rebels.
